headline: Romualdez Pleads Not Guilty in P7.4-Billion Plunder Case
seoTitle: Romualdez Pleads Not Guilty in P7.4-Billion Plunder Case | FMB News
seoDescription: Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez entered a not-guilty plea by videoconference in the P7.4-billion plunder case over alleged flood-control kickbacks.
deck: The former House speaker entered a not-guilty plea by videoconference from Quezon City Jail, moving the P7.4-billion plunder case into its next procedural stage. The charge remains an allegation and guilt has not been established.
author: FMB News Desk

continuesFrom.headline: Sandiganbayan Allows Romualdez to Attend Plunder Arraignment by Videoconference from Payatas Jail
continuesFrom.whatChanged: Romualdez has now been arraigned and entered a not-guilty plea, an independently newsworthy procedural development after the court's earlier videoconference order.

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Former House Speaker and Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez pleaded not guilty Wednesday to the P7.4-billion plunder charge filed against him and three others over alleged kickbacks linked to flood-control projects.

GMA News and the Philippine Daily Inquirer separately reported that Romualdez entered the plea by videoconference from his detention at the Quezon City Jail. The plea is a formal response to the charge and is not a determination of guilt.

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: FMB News earlier reported that the Sandiganbayan had allowed Romualdez to attend the September 16 arraignment remotely. The hearing has now taken place and a not-guilty plea has been entered, moving the case beyond the scheduling and custody stage covered in the earlier report.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Office of the Ombudsman has accused Romualdez and co-accused of plunder involving alleged kickbacks connected to flood-control and infrastructure projects. Romualdez has denied wrongdoing.
The allegations remain to be tested in court. FMB News does not present the filing of charges or the arraignment as proof of criminal liability.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Arraignment formally places the accused's plea on the record and allows the criminal case to proceed toward pre-trial and later stages. The case involves a former House speaker and allegations concerning billions of pesos in public infrastructure spending.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the pre-trial process, evidentiary disputes, prosecution and defense motions, and subsequent Sandiganbayan orders. Any claims by either side remain allegations unless established by evidence and court findings.

verificationNotes: GMA News reported the not-guilty plea at 10:34 a.m. PHT on September 16.
The Philippine Daily Inquirer independently reported the same plea.
The article explicitly distinguishes the criminal charge from established guilt.
This is a continuation of FMB News' 1:00 a.m. report because the actual plea is a material new procedural fact.
The contextual image is the same rights-cleared CC0 file photograph used in the earlier FMB report and is accurately labeled as a file image.
